fields.v: Lu, Z., Ren, H., Yang, Y., Wang, K., Zong, Z., Zhan, M., Li, H. (2026). FullStack-Agent: Enhancing Agentic Full-Stack Web Coding via Development-Oriented Testing and Repository Back-Translation. arXiv:2602.03798v1 [cs.SE], 3 Feb 2026. https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.03798
Preprint — arXiv:2602.03798v1 [cs.SE], 3 Feb 2026 ('Preprint. February 4, 2026'); no published venue stated

Multimedia Laboratory (MMLab), The Chinese University of Hong Kong (all); Shenzhen Loop Area Institute and Ace Robotics (Li). Corresponding author Zhan uses a sensetime.com address (company not listed as affiliation)

Proposes an approach; secondary: Proposes an evaluation method — FullStack-Agent: FullStack-Dev (multi-agent full-stack web development framework with planning, backend and frontend coding agents and dedicated debugging tools), FullStack-Learn (iterative self-improvement by repository back-translation and augmentation, SFT of the backbone LLM) and FullStack-Bench (benchmark with frontend, backend and database test cases and agent judges); compared with five agent baselines on two models, with ablations

FullStack-Dev (FullStack-Agent), no version; backbone LLMs Qwen3-Coder-480B-A35B-Instruct and Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct; fine-tuned FullStack-Learn-LM-round1 and -round2 (from Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct). Baselines (open-source implementations, versions/commits not stated): WebGen-Agent, TDDev, Bolt.diy, OpenHands, Qwen-Code

User instruction; template choice (Next.js frontend, NestJS backend; Vue.js and Django in an extension); Planning Agent output in JSON: backendPlan (entities with fields, apiEndpoints with method, path, request/response schemas typed to the finest granularity, status codes, businessRules, nonFunctional) and frontendPlan (pages, routes, layout, dataFlows, navigationLinks, sharedComponents); backend API summary (features implemented, successful API tests, demo data, known issues) passed to the frontend agent; generated repository

(1) Template selection and pure-frontend decision; (2) Planning Agent produces frontend and backend plans; (3) Backend Coding Agent implements the backend plan, validates all APIs with the backend debugging tool, injects demo data, writes a summary; (4) Frontend Coding Agent implements the frontend on the backend APIs and validates with the GUI-agent frontend debugging tool. Agents run in sandboxes; max 400 tool calls
None (fully automated pipeline)
Full workflow (automated generation from user instruction on FullStack-Bench), plus ablations removing the multi-agent mechanism and debugging tools
Not classifiable (closest to spec-first: a structured JSON plan is generated per run and drives the coding agents, not maintained afterwards); authors do not use SDD terms
New project: full-stack website generated from scratch (from a template) from a natural-language user instruction

FullStack-Bench: 101 user instructions (from WebGen-Bench), 647 frontend, 604 backend, 389 database test cases. Training: 2K trajectories from crawled GitHub repositories (round 1) + 8K from augmented repositories (round 2). Generated repository sizes Not stated
Web applications (full-stack websites: frontend, backend API, PostgreSQL database); TypeScript/JavaScript (Next.js, NestJS)
N/A (autonomous agents). Judge validation by four student volunteers with computer-science bachelor's degrees
None for generation (no tokens, time or money). Only: Backend Coding Agent average iterations 74.9 with vs 115.5 without the backend debugging tool. Training compute: 2 epochs on 32 H800 GPUs

FE Acc. = (N_YES + 0.5 × N_PARTIAL) / N_Total × 100% (GUI-agent judge); FE Acc. w/ Valid DB (YES/PARTIAL counted only if database-log check passes; main metric); BE Acc. and BE Acc. w/ Valid DB (share of YES backend API test cases); DB Acc. (share of YES database test cases on a schema snapshot)
None
None
Appearance Score (1-5, GUI-agent graded, following WebGen-Bench); human alignment accuracy of the judges; error taxonomy of failed cases (9 frontend, 4 backend, 4 database error types)

Automatic, by agent judges: frontend by a GUI agent with Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B-Instruct plus database-log validation; backend by a judge agent (Qwen3-Coder-480B-A35B-Instruct) that gathers API information and sends requests; database by a judge on a JSON snapshot (column names and first five rows). Manual: 200 sampled instances per test type checked by four student annotators; 300 error cases (50 per agent) manually categorised

All entries: quality verdict: no criterion stated by the authors; cost verdict: no criterion stated by the authors (cost not measured)

Benchmark: FullStack-Bench (101 instructions, 1,640 test cases). Configurations: 6 agent frameworks × 2 backbone LLMs; FullStack-Learn models on FullStack-Dev; ablations. Held constant: backbone LLM per comparison, instructions, test cases and judges; baselines wrapped in an explicit full-stack prompt (Fig. 2) because they default to frontend-only. FullStack-Dev: greedy decoding (temperature 0), context 131,072, max 400 tool calls; baseline run settings not stated beyond open-source implementations. Acceptance tests: agent-judged test cases (validated against humans). Repetitions: single run. No human intervention. Training data decontaminated against the benchmark (5-gram Jaccard > 0.6, embedding cosine > 0.7)

FullStack-Dev best with both models: 480B 64.7 / 77.8 / 77.9 (FE w/ DB / BE w/ DB / DB) vs WebGen-Agent 56.0 / 39.6 / 62.0, i.e. +8.7, +38.2, +15.9 points (OpenHands has the best baseline DB Acc., 72.5); 30B 37.2 / 38.7 / 50.9. Baselines' backend accuracies are far below frontend ones (mock data). FullStack-Learn round 2 improves the 30B model by +9.7, +9.5, +2.8 points; back-translated data beats directly generated trajectories. Ablations: removing the multi-agent mechanism lowers all metrics; each debugging tool mainly affects its own side. No significance tests

Distinguished configurations, and the database-validated metrics exposed frontend-only/mock-backend outputs that GUI-only metrics miss; judge reliability checked against humans (alignment 90.5% frontend, 94.0% backend, 97.5% database, 200 samples each). Repeatability not tested (single greedy run). Limitations of the comparison not stated by the authors, apart from using only two templates for stability

No limitations section. Gaps motivating the work: existing agents generate frontend-only sites masking missing backends; existing benchmarks (WebGen-Bench) judge only UI-level interactions. Impact statement: possible reduced demand for programmers and unclear responsibility for errors or vulnerabilities in agent-generated websites. Only two templates used for stability and compute

Inconsistencies: '+8.7%, 38.2%, 15.9%' over 'the previous state-of-the-art' are percentage points against WebGen-Agent, but OpenHands has a higher DB Acc. (72.5 vs 62.0), so the DB margin over the best baseline is 5.4 points (Table 2 vs abstract, p. 1, 6); model called 'Qwen3-Coder-30B-Instruct' (abstract, conclusion) vs 'Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct'; Table 3 row 'Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Inst.' is FullStack-Dev with the base model (same values as Table 2); extension (Table 8): the claimed increase holds for the main metrics (FE w/ Valid DB 64.7 to 68.1, BE w/ Valid DB 77.8 to 78.5, DB 77.9 to 81.0), but BE Acc. without the database check falls 83.4 to 80.5 and appearance 3.72 to 3.58. Values used: Tables 2-5, 8. Code released at https://github.com/mnluzimu/FullStack-Agent; baseline implementation code 'will' be released. WebGen-Agent and WebGen-Bench are the same authors' prior work. No pre-registration. Programming language: TypeScript/JavaScript (Next.js, NestJS); Python (Django) in the extension
fields.why: The draft called the Table 8 extension claim contradicted by the BE Acc. drop, but the paper's main metrics are the 'w/ Valid DB' ones (p. 6), and all three of them rise (p. 12). Only the secondary BE Acc. and the appearance score fall, so this is a minor point, not a contradiction.
